Beyond accurately identifying radioactivity levels from measurements of complicated spectra, spectralanalysisisalsoanimportanttechniquefordeterminingtherelativeradioactivityofdifferent isotopes within a sample or area containing radioactive material. The most obvious example of LBNL Report #2001653 such a use case is the determination and enrichment level when an unknown uranium sample is encountered. Determining the relative strengths of various isotopic peaks provides for relative emission rates which can be readily converted to isotopic ratios for samples subject to static measurements in controlled configurations [56]. However, during free-moving measurements, a detector system may encounter multiple different samples and often attenuation effects need to be accounted for (see previous section). If samples/areas of different enrichment cannot be isolated, commonly used tools would fail, however, coupling movement, enabled by SDF algorithms into enrichment analyses could overcome this CONOP limit.
